office_does: The State Senator is the 31st District's single member of the Washington Senate, voting on state law and budgets and confirming gubernatorial appointments.
race_blurb: Incumbent Republican Phil Fortunato, a senator since 2017, faces first-time Democratic candidate Tamara Stramel, a PTA and school-bond organizer. The race splits on spending, taxes, and school and family policy.

candidates.summary: Senator since 2017 and earlier a state representative, running on spending restraint, Second Amendment rights, and parental rights.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026 income tax over $1 million), ESHB 1296 (2025), and ESSB 5599 (2023) [S4][S5][S7]
Proposes zero-based budgeting and funding transportation without raising taxes [S3]
Endorsed by the Association of Washington Business and the King County Republican Party [S12][S13]

taxes.basis: Voted against the 2026 income tax and says families are being crushed by rising taxes; proposes funding transportation without new taxes.

spending.basis: Blames excessive spending and program growth, and proposes zero-based budgets and rolling back budget increases.

housing.basis: Blames regulations, fees, and land-use rules for a 'self-imposed housing crisis' and proposes opening up the state to build all kinds of housing.

safety.basis: Says sidewalk camping cannot be allowed and that people should be removed from the streets into treatment, alongside transitional housing.

local-control.basis: Proposes letting school districts waive costly state mandates.

experience.basis: Senator since 2017 with earlier House service, against a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Voted against ESSB 5599 on youth access to gender-affirming and reproductive care; no further statements found.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296's amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list and campaigns on defending parental rights.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate, Democratic precinct officer, and PTA and school-bond organizer from near Lake Tapps, running on infrastructure, school funding, and cost of living.
highlights: Wants the district prioritized in the transportation budget, including Fairfax Bridge funding [S1][S3]
Would change the school funding model and expand free school meals to all schools [S3]
Would support laws prohibiting surveillance and surge pricing [S3]

spending.basis: Says schools are asked to do more with less and calls for expanding free school meals and infrastructure investment.

experience.basis: First-time candidate whose only office is precinct committee officer, running against a long-serving senator.

tech.basis: Supports laws prohibiting surveillance and surge pricing that exploit customers.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no stated position on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.
